checks.label: What are the most interesting aspects of Perplexity that you're excited to work on?

checks.label: How do you use AI in your day-to-day work? What are some of the underappreciated benefits and/or pain points of your favorite AI tools?
checks.expected: In my current research engineering work, I use AI as an experimental collaborator and as a system component rather than as a black-box answer machine. At Arborphy, that means comparing visual encoders like BioCLIP, DINOv3, and EfficientNet, building a multi-agent botanical reasoning prototype with tool generation and evidence aggregation, and using reproducible evals to decide what actually improves recognition. My favorite tools are local and inspectable ones: Ollama for embedding a language model into a robot workflow, and Hugging Face/TransformerLens-style workflows for inspecting model behavior. The underappreciated benefit is faster iteration when the model is close to the data and the evaluation loop is explicit. The pain point is that models can look persuasive while adding no measurable value: I have seen fusion fail to beat BioCLIP alone, and hallucination-circuit work break down because behavior was unstable and first-token evidence was too weak.
